newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper miners accept Sunday shifts.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper miners accept Sunday shifts.

text.p: Workers at Portugal's Neves Corvo copper miner voted on Thursday "not to reject" a management proposal on Sunday working and union leaders said the new system would go into force from next week.
Union leaders said talks would continue with management on certain aspects of the deal as well as the company's commitment to creating 100 new jobs.
"We are going to wait for the new jobs to be created and then we will review the situation," union leader Eduardo Lazaro told Reuters by telephone from the mine.

Some 300 miners, members of the morning and afternoon shifts, voted on a deal hammered out on Monday by union leaders and management that would ensure continuous working at the 107,000 tonnes per year mine 250 km south of Lisbon.
Somincor, the state-owned company which operates the mine, says continuous working is needed to boost efficiency and counter falling ore yields.
Members of the night shift would take a vote later on Thursday but union officials said that the result was likely to be the same.
